A cube root is defined for every real number, so its domain is $\mathbb{R}$. $y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3 - x}}$ is incorrect. The square root is in a denominator, so $3 - x > 0$, that is $x < 3$, so its domain is $(-\infty, 3)$. $y = \ln(x - 3)$ is incorrect. The logarithm needs $x - 3 > 0$, so its domain is $(3, +\infty)$.
form: Which function has the given domain (reverse form)

The square root is in a denominator, so $x + 3 > 0$, so its domain is $(-3, +\infty)$.
